title: The system: a public API platform with rate limiting at the edge
caption: Every request crosses one gateway that knows the rules and asks a shared counter cluster; services behind it only see traffic within budget.

steps.text: Requests from apps and partners hit the edge first. The WAF drops obvious junk (known-bad IPs, malformed requests) before it costs anything.
The gateway keeps the limit rules in memory (per API key, tier and endpoint) and hot-reloads them from a config store: no lookup per request.
Per request: build the key (api_key:endpoint) and make one atomic call to the counter cluster, about 1 ms.
Allowed: route to the service. Orders, search and auth and their databases only ever see traffic within budget.
Over the limit: 429 with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining, returned through the edge.
Emit metrics: rejects per key, keys near their limit, counter latency. A spike of 429s means a client bug or an attack.

scenarios.name: Bot flood
scenarios.summary: A credential-stuffing burst on /login: the WAF takes the obvious part, per-key limits take the rest, and services never notice.

steps.text: 200 000 req/s of login attempts arrive from rotating IPs.
The WAF blocks known-bad IP ranges; what's left reaches the gateway.
The strict login rule (5 per minute per account and per IP) rejects almost everything after one atomic call each.
Auth sees normal load. The 429 spike on /login pages the on-call engineer.

scenarios.name: Counter shard down
scenarios.summary: Decide per route: fail open where availability matters, fail closed where abuse is the bigger cost.

steps.text: One shard of the counter cluster stops answering; calls for keys on it time out after 5 ms.
Orders and search fail open: requests go through unprotected for keys on that shard.
Login fails closed: it returns 503 rather than let a brute-force attack through.
Alert, promote the shard's replica, and the counters resume (they may restart near zero for a minute).

scenarios.name: Rule change
scenarios.summary: A partner upgrades to a 10× tier: change the rule, not the code. Gateways pick it up within seconds.

steps.text: An operator raises partner P's limit from 1 000 to 10 000 per minute in the config store.
Every gateway reloads the rules (push or poll every few seconds). No deploy.
P's next requests are checked against the new limit; the key and the counter don't change.
